changed.title: Exact passing-key count for a cyclic Boolean row test at one round from 8 bits and two rounds from 16 bits
changed.statement:
∀ (k r u : Nat) (c : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k)), u < 2 ^ k →
  ((r = 1 ∧ 8 ≤ k) ∨ (r = 2 ∧ 16 ≤ k)) →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (x : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (x.testBit i)
        (!(x.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && x.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let state := fun (w : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun prev j =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * j) w ^^^ (c (j + 1)).val)
      (rot 1 w ^^^ u)
  ((List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun key => decide (state key < 2 ^ (k - (k + 1) / 2)))).length =
    2 ^ (k - (k + 1) / 2)
changed.unlocks: the number of passing keys for a fixed row in the one-round and two-round circuit constructions
changed.context: On paper. Change variables to the rotated key XOR the row. A tested bit at i equals a pivot bit XOR a function of the four bits to its right at one round, or eight at two. Rotate indices by one or two. Put all free positions before the pivots, then process the pivots in descending order. Each needed operand is set already or wraps into the free prefix. Complete each prefix uniquely, invert the rotation and XOR, and count the prefixes. Circuit-price companions cannot exist for an exact count of passing keys with no circuit size in its statement.

Rotate indices by one or two. Put all free positions before the pivots, then process the pivots in descending order. Each needed operand is set already or wraps into the free prefix. Complete each prefix uniquely, invert the rotation and XOR, and count the prefixes. Circuit-price companions cannot exist for an exact count of passing keys with no circuit size in its statement.

changed.title: A Boolean rule that determines each later bit from its prefix has exactly one completion per free prefix
changed.statement:
∀ (free forced : ℕ)
  (rule : (i : Fin forced) → (Fin free → Bool) → (Fin i.val → Bool) → Bool),
  let freeBits := fun (word : Fin (free + forced) → Bool) (a : Fin free) =>
    word (Fin.castAdd forced a)
  let passes := fun (word : Fin (free + forced) → Bool) =>
    ∀ i : Fin forced, word (Fin.natAdd free i) =
      rule i (freeBits word)
        (fun j => word (Fin.natAdd free (Fin.castLE (Nat.le_of_lt i.isLt) j)))
  ∃ complete : (Fin free → Bool) ≃ { word // passes word },
    (∀ seed word, freeBits word.val = seed ↔ word = complete seed) ∧
    Nat.card { word // passes word } = 2 ^ free
changed.unlocks: counting all keys from the free bits in the one-round and two-round rules
changed.context: On paper. Fix the free prefix. Recursively assign each forced bit from the free prefix and the earlier forced bits. Apply the recursion equation at each forced index to verify the rule. Taking its free prefix recovers the seed. For the other inverse, induct on the forced index. A passing word and the word rebuilt from its prefix have identical earlier bits, so the rule prescribes the same next bit. Transfer cardinality across this equivalence and count Boolean functions on Fin f. The empty prefix gives one completion.

A passing word and the word rebuilt from its prefix have identical earlier bits, so the rule prescribes the same next bit. Transfer cardinality across this equivalence and count Boolean functions on Fin f. The empty prefix gives one completion.

changed.statement: ¬ (∃ ρ : List (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin (4 + 1) × Fin 4)), PEqualNP.Search.IsRUPRun (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PHP (4 + 1) 4) ρ ∧ (∅ : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin (4 + 1) × Fin 4)) ∈ ρ ∧ ρ.length ≤ 12)

changed.statement: ¬ (∃ π : List (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.LinClause (Fin 5 × Fin 2)), PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsLinRefutation (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.BPHP 5 2) π ∧ π.length ≤ 127)
